scripts.purpose: SKELETON - not implemented. Runs on this machine and invokes each host in REMOTE_SERVERS to execute that host's installed backup.sh, so each server creates its own local archive instead of sending data here. Expected outcome: after a successful run an archive matching $BACKUP_DIR/$ARCHIVE_HEADER-<timestamp>.tar.gz exists on each server, verified by a remote path check. Planned behavior: help and config-file options exit before any SSH; every host is attempted; a failed host is reported without hiding the others; a nonzero exit means at least one host failed. Open questions: whether to pass --dry-run or --notify-send through to the remote backup, whether a per-host timeout should override SSH_TIMEOUT, and whether remote output is collected or streamed.

arguments.name: -h|--help
arguments.description: Print usage and exit 0 before contacting any host.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; takes precedence over USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG and installed/legacy/repository lookup. A missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: REMOTE_SERVERS
environment.description: Array of user@host targets; an empty list makes this script a no-op that exits 0.

environment.name: REMOTE_INSTALL_DIR
environment.description: Directory on each server where backup.sh is installed; planned command path.

environment.name: SSH_TIMEOUT
environment.description: Non-interactive ssh connect timeout in seconds.

write_paths: on each server: $BACKUP_DIR/$ARCHIVE_HEADER-<timestamp>.tar.gz (created by that server's backup.sh)

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed, or every configured host ran its backup successfully and a newly created archive is present on that server under $BACKUP_DIR; an empty REMOTE_SERVERS is also success.
Config file unreadable, or at least one host could not be reached or its backup exited nonzero.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.
